title: Cultivating Pluriversal Politics in art workshops to reach Post-growth Transformations
venue: Suomen antropologi: Journal of the Finnish Anthropological Society
why: Uses anticolonial artistic practice to open pluriversal space inside a growth-bound institution. The closest thing this week to a method for pluralising your own workshops.
caveat: An anthropological argument from workshop practice. No transferable evaluation is offered.
abstract: The current moment is witnessing a range of human-made problems, the consequences of which are felt most by those who have contributed the least to them. Institutional arrangements still prioritise a model of limitless growth. Drawing on pluriversal politics in this article, I argue that anticolonial artistic practices can offer tools to support post-growth transformations by creating spaces for alternative modes of being and doing that challenge the logics of separation. Here, I provide an examination of artistic methods used in workshops led by dancer Ana Kavalis and visual artist Rosamaría Bolom, respectively, through embodied participant observation. Both artists used different sensory techniques intended to expand the notion of the body into a collective, relational entity. Ana Kavalis’s workshop, Corpo Migrante: Corpo Ressonante (‘Migrant Body: Resonant Body’), encouraged bodily contemplation of how one perceives the world, while Rosamaría Bolom’s workshop, Corpas Que Voam (‘Bodies That Fly’), demonstrated how convivial collective spaces that use acuerpamiento provide autonomous ways to challenge power. I conclude this article arguing that the anthropologist’s sensory approach is broadly urgent for facilitating transformative change.
